s1.syndrome_frame: Widespread skin condition with progressive worsening and characteristic plaques
salient_findings: Widespread polycyclic serpiginous, erythematous plaques with a double-edged scale
key_facts: The patient is a 32-year-old woman
The skin condition has progressively worsened
The condition involves 90% of her body surface area (BSA)
Polycyclic serpiginous, erythematous plaques are present on the trunk and extremities
The plaques involve 30% of the body surface area (BSA)
Eyebrow hairs are sparse and less than 5 mm long
Scalp hairs are coarse and brittle
Skin biopsy showed psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia with spongiosis
Trichography showed nodal swelling, with invagination of the distal hair into the proximal end

raw.syndrome_frame: Widespread skin condition with progressive worsening and characteristic plaques
salient_findings: Widespread polycyclic serpiginous, erythematous plaques with a double-edged scale
key_facts: The patient is a 32-year-old woman
The skin condition has progressively worsened
The condition involves 90% of her body surface area (BSA)
Polycyclic serpiginous, erythematous plaques are present on the trunk and extremities
The plaques involve 30% of the body surface area (BSA)
Eyebrow hairs are sparse and less than 5 mm long
Scalp hairs are coarse and brittle
Skin biopsy showed psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia with spongiosis
Trichography showed nodal swelling, with invagination of the distal hair into the proximal end

raw.rationale: The presence of widespread polycyclic serpiginous, erythematous plaques with a double-edged scale, sparse and short eyebrow hairs, and coarse and brittle scalp hairs, along with the skin biopsy showing psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia with spongiosis, are consistent with Pityriasis rubra pilaris. Additionally, the trichography results showing nodal swelling with invagination of the distal hair into the proximal end support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Psoriasis vulgaris
rejected.why: While the skin biopsy shows psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia, the clinical presentation and trichography results are more suggestive of Pityriasis rubra pilaris

rejected.label: Erythroderma
rejected.why: Erythroderma typically presents with widespread redness and scaling, but the specific findings of polycyclic serpiginous plaques and hair abnormalities are not typical

rejected.label: Pustular psoriasis
rejected.why: Pustular psoriasis is characterized by the presence of pustules, which are not mentioned in the case description

rejected.label: Guttate psoriasis
rejected.why: Guttate psoriasis typically presents with small, droplike lesions, which do not match the description of the patient's plaques
